narrativeReportMd:
# GraphDefinition R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`GraphDefinition` is absent from the R6 core package, so R4 instances with `resourceType: "GraphDefinition"` have no same-core R6 StructureDefinition and are hard-breaking at the resource identity level.

## Scope
The analysis compared the R4 `GraphDefinition` StructureDefinition with the supplied R6 core package. Because the assigned R6 StructureDefinition file is missing, I searched the R6 package index and local StructureDefinition/OperationDefinition artifacts for a renamed, split, merged, or removed counterpart. No in-core replacement resource was found. R6 operation documentation references an external API-incubator `GraphDefinition`, but that external artifact is outside the supplied core package.

## Main migration themes
The migration concern is wholesale model loss rather than a narrow field rename. R4 `GraphDefinition` carries canonical metadata, a mandatory `name`, `status`, and `start`, and a recursive `link.target.link` graph with target profiles, reverse lookup parameters, and compartment-consistency rules. R6 core does not define where those concepts live. Systems that still need graph definitions will likely need a non-core dependency, implementation-guide profile, extension strategy, or custom transform.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is the core resource removal/externalization. A second high-impact consequence is that all local GraphDefinition elements lose direct R6 core representation. A narrower terminology finding covers the GraphDefinition-specific compartment-use and compartment-rule bindings, whose R4 CodeSystems and ValueSets are absent from R6 core.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed to decide whether to depend on the API-incubator artifact, keep R4 GraphDefinition resources as legacy data, or map the graph definition into implementation-specific configuration. The local package evidence is strong for absence from R6 core, but it does not include the external StructureDefinition or official migration rationale.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Because R4 `GraphDefinition` was trial-use/FMM 1, removing it from core may be justified, especially if the model moved to an incubator IG. A less disruptive path would have retained a deprecated compatibility StructureDefinition in core or shipped a ConceptMap/cross-version extension to preserve old resources during migration.

## Follow-up analysis
Review the HL7 API-incubator GraphDefinition artifact and the reports for related operations/search parameters. Also review base-resource reports separately for inherited Resource/DomainResource changes; those are intentionally excluded here.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `GraphDefinition` is not present in the R6 core package, so R4 `GraphDefinition` instances are hard-breaking for core R6 validation. The top migration concerns are loss of the resource identity, loss of the recursive graph/link content model, and absence of the graph-specific compartment terminology from R6 core. The main uncertainty is whether the external API-incubator `GraphDefinition` referenced by R6 operation documentation is the intended replacement.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is likely a dependency/modeling decision rather than an element-by-element transform. Implementers must decide whether to keep R4 `GraphDefinition` as legacy configuration, adopt the external API-incubator artifact, or express graph traversal rules in implementation-specific configuration, profiles, or extensions. Existing code generators and validators that enumerate FHIR core resource types need to remove or quarantine `GraphDefinition` for R6 core, while preserving any historical R4 data that still drives graph operations.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that `GraphDefinition` is absent from R6 core: the assigned file is missing, the R6 package index has no exact StructureDefinition entry, local StructureDefinition searches found no semantic replacement, and related R4 graph-specific artifacts are not present in R6 core. Confidence is lower for replacement guidance because the supplied inputs do not include the external API-incubator StructureDefinition, official change rationale, narrative migration notes, or ConceptMaps.

findings.narrativeMd: `GraphDefinition` disappeared from the R6 core resource set. This is the most direct form of breaking change: existing R4 graph-definition resources cannot be revalidated as core R6 resources, and generated R6 models will normally not include a `GraphDefinition` class or `ResourceType.GraphDefinition` enum value. The R6 core package still contains references to GraphDefinition in operation documentation, but those references do not provide a core StructureDefinition.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance with `resourceType: "GraphDefinition"` becomes invalid or unprocessable for core R6 validators because the resource type is unknown. Strict parsers may reject it at dispatch, code generators may omit the class, and servers may no longer advertise or accept it as a core resource. There is no core R6-to-R4 instance shape to map back; only non-core/incubator content would create a reverse-mapping question.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory stored or configured `GraphDefinition` resources before moving to R6. Decide whether to retain them as R4 legacy artifacts, adopt the external API-incubator definition, or convert them into server-specific graph traversal configuration. Validation test suites should include unknown-resource handling and any operation/document-assembly paths that previously accepted a GraphDefinition canonical.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change may be justified by the resource's low maturity and possible incubator migration, but a compatibility StructureDefinition or formal migration map would have been less disruptive. Without that, downstream systems must make local policy decisions and cannot rely on the R6 core package alone for validation or code generation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against official ballot notes or the API-incubator package before finalizing migration advice. The local R6 package evidence proves absence from core but not the intended replacement contract.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 GraphDefinition was a real core resource, and R6 core no longer publishes a StructureDefinition for it. An R4 instance with resourceType `GraphDefinition` will not validate or dispatch as a core R6 resource, and generated R6 models will normally omit the type. That is a real break for implementers who used GraphDefinition with graph, document, or validation workflows. I would not mark it Revisit on the available evidence because the resource was FMM 1/trial-use, the R6 package points toward external/incubator handling rather than a simple in-core rename, and quick checks did not establish broad production dependence. The remaining R6 operation text that references GraphDefinition is migration-relevant, but retaining a deprecated core resource would keep an experimental model in core and risk duplicate core/incubator representations.

That would preserve R4 validation, but it has material tradeoffs: continued maintenance of FMM 1 core content, duplicate representations, ambiguous operation targets, and lingering implementer support burden.

findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Existing R4 instances fail R6 core validation at the resource-type level, and every local GraphDefinition element is therefore also unrecognized. findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Treat migration as a graph-rule modeling exercise. Extract required R4 fields (`name`, `status`, `start`) and traversal rules (`link`, `target`, `compartment`) into the chosen replacement: an external GraphDefinition package, server configuration, or custom extension-bearing artifact. Test at least simple one-hop links, recursive target links, profile-constrained targets, and compartment rule behavior.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A field-by-field backward-compatible alternative would have been straightforward only if `GraphDefinition` remained in core. Once the resource was removed, old element compatibility requires a wrapper, extension set, or external dependency. Such alternatives are possible but would have shifted complexity from core maintainers to validators and implementers.

A server or tool that used `GraphDefinition.start`, `GraphDefinition.link`, target profiles, or compartment rules must migrate that graph configuration into an external package or non-core server configuration. That is real path-level migration work, but it is derivative of the resource-level removal rather than a separate design issue. Given FMM 1/trial-use, carrying all 32 legacy local paths in base R6 is only justified if the resource itself stays in core.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is not a direct local `GraphDefinition` element change because the assigned R6 core StructureDefinition is absent and `Composition/$document` is a separate OperationDefinition. It is nevertheless important identity evidence.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Composition/$document` documentation links to this external GraphDefinition. It should be inspected to determine whether it is the intended successor and whether it preserves R4 local elements and terminology.

R4 had a Resource `$graph` operation based on GraphDefinition, while the R6 core package only has `$graphql` among similarly named Resource operations. Operation-level compatibility should be assessed separately.

R4 defines a GraphDefinition `start` search parameter. Because the base resource is absent from R6 core, search-parameter migration and capability-statement effects should be handled in the search-parameter/operation analysis.
Inherited base-artifact changes were intentionally excluded from this GraphDefinition report and should be read from the corresponding base artifact reports if they affect runtime migration.
